figures.denominator_def: pre-IND months / total months from programme start to approval
figures.sample: derived from the cited input evidence records

derivation: DiMasi: 31.2 / (31.2 + 96.8) = 31.2/128.0 = 0.2438 -> 24.4% (inputs E-1005). Sertkaya: 31.2 / (31.2+27.8+34.0+38.0+16.2) = 31.2/147.2 = 0.2120 -> 21.2% (inputs E-1014). Paul: (12+18+24+12) / (12+18+24+12+18+30+30+18) = 66/162 = 0.4074 -> 40.7% (inputs E-1017). Paul is higher because its clock starts at target selection while DiMasi's starts at compound synthesis.

claim: H0-c Amdahl ceiling: driving all pre-IND work to zero duration would cut total elapsed development time by at most 21 to 41 percent, and would cut capitalized cost per approval by at most 40 to 43 percent but out-of-pocket cash cost by only 7 to 31 percent.
source_title: Derived calculation by RLSX Agent A

figures.denominator_def: maximum achievable reduction in total time / cost if the pre-IND stage duration and outlay both go to zero
figures.sample: derived from the cited input evidence records

derivation: Time ceiling = preIND_share_of_elapsed_time (E-1093): 21.2%-40.7%. Cost ceiling, capitalized = E-1090 (42.9%) and E-1013 (40.2%). Cost ceiling, out-of-pocket = E-1013 (6.8%) to E-1091 (30.8%). Note the capitalized ceiling is not fully attainable even in principle: part of the pre-IND capitalized burden is compounding on clinical-stage attrition, which only falls if PoS rises, not if discovery gets faster (see H0-b).

claim: Novel US drug approvals per billion nominal dollars of PhRMA member R&D fell from 1.11 in 2000 to 0.41 in 2010, recovered to 0.58 in 2020 and stood at 0.37 in 2022.
source_title: Derived calculation by RLSX Agent A

figures.denominator_def: US novel drug approvals in year t divided by PhRMA member total R&D in year t, nominal dollars
figures.sample: derived from the cited input evidence records

derivation: 2000: 29 / 26.0308 = 1.114. 2010: 21 / 50.7098 = 0.414. 2020: 53 / 91.1263 = 0.582. 2022: 37 / 100.8452 = 0.367. Inputs: E-1038 (approvals), E-1041 (R&D). THREE DENOMINATOR CAVEATS: (i) nominal dollars, no deflator applied; (ii) the numerator counts approvals from all sponsors while the denominator covers PhRMA members only, and the non-member share of approvals has grown; (iii) spend in year t does not produce the approval in year t, so this ratio is not a productivity estimate and must not be read as one.

claim: On PhRMA's 2022 categorised outlays, pre-human work absorbed 19.9 percent of member R&D and Phase III alone absorbed 36.1 percent.
source_title: Derived calculation by RLSX Agent A

figures.denominator_def: pre-human R&D / (total R&D minus uncategorised), single-year outlay basis
figures.sample: derived from the cited input evidence records

derivation: 15.9 / 80.0 = 0.1988 -> 19.9%. Phase III: 28.8 / 80.0 = 0.360 -> 36.0%; using dollars 29050.3 / (100845.2 - 20147.0) = 29050.3/80698.2 = 0.3600 -> 36.0%. Input: E-1042. This is a flow measure of where a year's cash goes, not a per-approval attribution, and it does not carry attrition or cost of capital.
